case_name: Archna Sharma vs Suresh Kumar Sharma

parties.petitioner_plaintiff: wife, seeking divorce on ground of cruelty
parties.respondent_defendant: husband, seeking divorce on ground of cruelty

facts_of_case: Marriage between the parties took place in Delhi. The couple had a child. The husband alleged that the wife was cruel to him and used derogatory remarks. She went to her parental home with the child without his consent. Her mother came to Rohtak, hurled abuses, and threatened to take away her daughter and child.

legal_principles.principle: Unsubstantiated allegations cannot be used as a ground for granting relief to the husband.
legal_principles.held: These allegations appear to have been made in the written statement for the first time but the question is whether these unsubstantiated allegations could be made a part of the cause in order to grant relief to the husband who sought divorce on the ground of cruelty, without making these allegations as a part of the divorce petition initially.

legal_principles.principle: The cumulative effect of certain matters can be taken into consideration while deciding a case.
legal_principles.held: In order to conclude that the husband has succeeded in proving the acts of the respondent which amounted to mental cruelty seems to have taken into condition the cumulative effect of certain matters which are discussed herein-thereafter.

outcome.final_order: Marriage between the parties was dissolved by a decree of divorce.

use_for_drafting: drafting a petition for divorce under Hindu Marriage Act
